messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — there's a runtime hotfix that needs rolling to prod tonight within the 00:00-02:00 UTC change window. Thinking we do a patch-only service bump (no dep bumps). Agree?
kevin: What commit range? Is this limited to the serving runtime container or runtime+agents?
maria: Only serving runtime binary + a small config tweak (kv cache TTL). I'll paste diff in a sec. Change window confirmed.
maria: diff: ```git diff --stat HEAD~3..HEAD
 runtime/serve.cc | 12 +++++++++---
 config/kv.yml | 2 +-
 ...
```
deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary to eu-west-1 (release/2139991111-hotfix). Logs: https://builds.redwood/run/2139991111
jen: For tagging — i'd prefer an annotated semver tag `v1.12.3` and a CI buildmeta tag `v1.12.3+ci.213999` instead of creating a separate 'hotfix' semver variant. Keeps npm/pip semantics sane.
sam: Slight pushback — annotated tags are great but lockfile consumers (yarn/poetry) sometimes prefer explicit patch bumps in package metadata so lock resolution is deterministic. If we only add buildmeta (+ci...) some package managers ignore it.
olga: From PM/product side — customers see version strings in telemetry. We should avoid extra confusing suffixes. If we use buildmeta, ensure release notes clarify.
kevin: Operationally, pinning the service to `v1.12.3` (patch) and shipping an internal buildmeta is fine. For the repo we should `git tag -a v1.12.3 -m "runtime patch: kv ttl fix"` then push. npm: `npm version patch --no-git-tag-version` then `git commit -am 'bump pkg to v1.12.3'` then `git tag -a v1.12.3+ci.213999 -m 'ci build'` — or we can keep buildmeta only in CI artifacts.
jen: Agree. Also recommend annotated tag for releases and keep `+ci` only on the container image tag like `registry.redwood/v1.12.3+ci213999`
deploy-bot: Canary finished: 3/3 health checks passed, latency p95: 120ms, errors: 0. Promote? (reaction required)
kevin: Promote.
maria: Decision: annotated semver tag v1.12.3 for repo, container image with `+ci` metadata, don't modify package lockfiles, add explicit pin in Dedicated config for the next 7 days. Rollback plan in case of regressions: revert to `v1.12.2` and redeploy all zones, documented below.
kevin: Rollback snippet: ```bash
git tag -d v1.12.3 || true
git push origin :refs/tags/v1.12.3 || true
git checkout v1.12.2
./scripts/deploy --target prod --force --tag v1.12.2
```
sam: :thumbsup: 
jen: I'll open a tiny PR to add "release.meta" to the release notes template (fields: semver, image_tag, build_id, change_window).
maria: Thanks — assigning jen. I'll post the release note + changelog after CI finishes. Note: if anything flakey during canary, we abort and follow rollback.
olga: Can you add a short customer-facing note? Two lines max.
maria: Will do. ETA 30m.
